title: Thumbnails: add unlimitedStorage + switch capture to WebP
description:
background.js captureTab() writes base64 JPEG data URLs to chrome.storage.local, but the manifest requests "storage" WITHOUT "unlimitedStorage" (~10MB cap). When the quota is exceeded, set() rejects, the surrounding catch swallows it with only a console.warn, and thumbnails silently stop persisting. There is also no eviction cap on total thumb_* keys (only per-tab cleanup on close).

Do:
1. Add "unlimitedStorage" to manifest permissions.
2. Switch captureVisibleTab format from "jpeg" to "webp" for economy (chrome.tabs.captureVisibleTab supports "webp"); tune quality. Also update SettingsPanel.js resizeToDataUrl (custom background) to canvas.toDataURL("image/webp", ...) for the same reason.
3. Consider an LRU/size cap on cached thumbnails as a backstop even with unlimitedStorage.
Verify thumbnails still render across many tabs and that storage no longer silently fails.
label: Maintenance

activity.content:
Implemented thumbnail storage hardening and WebP conversion.

- Added `unlimitedStorage` to the extension manifest.
- Switched tab captures to WebP at quality 55 and custom background resizing to WebP.
- Routed captures through the shared thumbnail cache, capped at 200 entries / approximately 50 MiB with least-recently-captured eviction.
- Kept cache recency metadata synchronized when tabs close.
- Added tests covering WebP resizing, 200-tab cache pruning, and eviction metadata cleanup.

Validation: `node --test` (6/6 passing), `node --check background.js`, `node --check utils/thumbnailCache.js`, manifest JSON parse, and `git diff --check` all passed.
